summary: Polygon's annual Halloween Countdown is a daily calendar of 31 horror or Halloween-adjacent movies and TV picks from staff, each with a short review and streaming locations. This fourth edition runs from Messiah of Evil on Oct. 1 to The Exorcist III on Oct. 31. It mixes classics, cult films, international horror, shorts, and TV episodes, all watchable at home.
one_line: Polygon's 2023 Halloween Countdown gives one staff-recommended horror movie, show, or short per day for October, with where to stream each.
key_facts: Polygon has made a Halloween countdown calendar for the past three years, and this year's edition has a whole new batch of 31 picks, one added each day in October.
Oct. 1 pick Messiah of Evil is a ’70s cosmic horror film by Willard Huyck and Gloria Katz, set in the coastal town of Point Dume, California, where townspeople turn into flesh-eating ghouls.
Oct. 2 pick Ginger Snaps was directed by future Orphan Black co-creator John Fawcett and is a werewolf story about two sisters that works as a puberty allegory.
Oct. 3 pick Creepshow is available on Kanopy; the new 4K UHD Blu-ray release made Polygon's list of the best Blu-rays of 2023, and Stephen King performs as a hillbilly in it.
Oct. 4 pick Pulse is Kiyoshi Kurosawa's post-Y2K J-horror film about the dead spilling into the world through the internet, produced after Kurosawa's Cure, which was on last year's calendar.
Oct. 6 pick Dracula 2000 stars Gerard Butler as Dracula, was written and directed by Patrick Lussier, and is a Dimension Films movie; its sequel is Dracula II: Ascension.
Oct. 9 pick The Scooby-Doo Project is a Blair Witch Project parody starring Mystery Inc., originally made as a bumper for a 1999 Scooby-Doo marathon before Cartoon Network aired it as a movie.

Oct. 10 pick Saloum is a Senegalese thriller directed by Jean Luc Herbulot, running 84 minutes, which premiered at the 2021 Toronto International Film Festival and won awards at Fantastic Fest and the Vancouver International Film Festival.
Oct. 11 pick Heck is Kyle Edward Ball's 2020 short film, conceived as a proof of concept for his feature debut Skinamarink.

Oct. 12 pick Harper's Island is a 13-episode slasher TV miniseries from 2009 in which Abby (Elaine Cassidy) returns to the island for her friend Henry's wedding, with episode titles that are onomatopoeias for how people die.
Oct. 14 pick Cat People, directed by Jacques Tourneur and running 73 minutes, is credited with originating the modern jump scare, the 'Lewton Bus' named after producer Val Lewton.
Oct. 16 pick Project Wolf Hunting is a Korean 'Con Air meets Predator' monster film whose director has bragged that the team used 2.5 tons of fake blood.

Oct. 21 pick is Luca Guadagnino's 2018 Suspiria, with Tilda Swinton in multiple roles, cinematography by Sayombhu Mukdeeprom, and a score by Thom Yorke; it is recommended as a double feature with Dario Argento's 1977 original, which Criterion Collection was making available.
Oct. 22 pick Pan's Labyrinth is Guillermo del Toro's fairy tale set after the Spanish Civil War, starring Ivana Baquero as Ofelia, Sergi López as Captain Vidal, and Doug Jones as the Faun.

Oct. 31 pick The Exorcist III was written and directed by William Peter Blatty; Morgan Creek Productions demanded he reshoot the final act, which originally ended without an exorcism, and John Carpenter was once tapped to direct.
